digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verified CI on GitHub Actions
propositions: macOS CI execution time doubled from 15-20 minutes to 30-40 minutes; regression transition identified at commit ceea743 (2026-08-01) to 7a1863f with +14m31s pytest execution growth driven by ~4.1k additional test lines and nine expensive test mechanics (long timeouts, real sleeps, repeated AST parsing, wiki corpus recomputation, and production-scale socket/process operations).

Mutation testing added at e0b3fdfc8e (2026-08-12) increased aggregate runner usage when selected but was skipped in 57 of 62 post-landing runs; analysis of 62 runs shows active-mutation averaged 33.0m wall vs skipped runs 36.5m, proving mutation is not the direct cause of the observed latency regression.

Seven performance remediations identified: fake clock for 120s JIRA readiness timeout, late-bound sleep injection for Jira capability and dependency audit, immutable AST cache per-process, per-session wiki corpus cache, import_tickets optimization at N=3000, source/base fixture reuse, and reduced test-only real socket/process timing windows; all preserve coverage and existing accepted test contracts.

GitHub Free org resource limits (20 total jobs / 5 macOS) amplify deterministic test work through subprocess/APFS contention under process saturation; prior runner parallelism proposals rejected as not reducing aggregate consumption.

Existing telemetry (pytest --durations=25 logs) contained sufficient observability to decompose the regression into workflow queue time, job queue time, and execution critical path; no observability code changes required.

Root cause confirmed as combined effect of test volume growth, expensive per-test mechanics (captured sleeps, real timeouts, repeated compilation), and contention amplification under macOS resource limits; mutation testing materially increases usage but does not explain the regression present across 57 skipped-mutation runs.
